query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of a refractory metal such as Ta or W to the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy will improve its integrity and strength without sacrificing its caloric response.
generation.intervention: Addition of a refractory metal such as Ta or W
generation.conditions: Applied-field and pressure-field operation, high temperatures
generation.structural_mediator: Solid-solution strengthening and formation of hard Laves phases
generation.mechanism: The refractory metal addition will lead to solid-solution strengthening and the formation of hard Laves phases, which will improve the alloy's strength and integrity.
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved compressive strength and integrity, potentially exceeding 1000 MPa, without a significant decrease in caloric response
generation.baseline: As-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy with poor integrity and tendency to crack
generation.boundary: The alloy's performance under applied-field and pressure-field operation, high temperatures, and loading regimes will be evaluated
generation.uncertainty: The exact amount of refractory metal to be added and the optimal processing conditions to achieve the desired properties are uncertain

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy samples with and without the addition of a refractory metal such as Ta or W, and evaluate their compressive strength, integrity, and caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation, high temperatures, and loading regimes
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the addition of a refractory metal such as Ta or W does not improve the alloy's integrity and strength without sacrificing its caloric response, the hypothesis is falsified

We present a comprehensive theoretical and experimental study of the compression and deformation behavior of prototypical high-entropy transition metal boride (Hf, Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti)B2 and (Hf, Mo, Nb, Ta, Zr)B2 samples to high pressures and high temperatures. The high-pressure, high-temperature synthesis and compression studies of high-entropy transition metal borides are carried out in the same sample chamber, thereby minimizing exposure to ambient environments. The hexagonal AlB2 phase of both high-entropy boride samples was found to be stable to pressure and temperature conditions of 9.5 GPa and 2273 K, respectively. The supercell approach using the stochastic (or special) quasi-random structure (SQS) predicts a bulk modulus value of 288 GPa, in excellent agreement with the measured value of 276 GPa. The changes in bulk modulus and thermal expansion coefficient with temperatures were also documented in this study. The compressive strength of the (Hf, Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti)B2 sample approaches a value of 28 GPa at an applied pressure of 65 GPa in a measurement carried out in a diamond anvil cell.
